key_idea: Reverse the process: each exposure peels one layer, so the answer is the maximum 4-neighbour BFS distance from a cookie cell to the nearest non-cookie cell or pan border.
sketch: Cells that have a non-cookie neighbour or lie on the pan boundary get layer 1 and seed a multi-source BFS; every other cookie cell gets 1 + min of its neighbours. The maximum layer is the answer: layer d cells cannot be chipified before round d (lower bound), and placing dough on all cells of layer >= d' progressively achieves it. O(nm). Pitfall: the pan border counts as exposed, and the shape can be disconnected.
